title: Were you there?
hookLine: a spiritual asking: were you there when they crucified my Lord?
carry: sometimes it causes me to tremble
tomorrow: why would a song about going home name a river, and a campground?

lines: NOT DID IT HAPPEN: WERE YOU THERE?
cards: Rehearsal is running late. The piano stops, the director lowers her hands, and one voice is left in the room, nothing under it, singing toward the empty pews: “Were you there when they crucified my Lord?”
Not, did it happen. Not, what does it mean. Were you there.
The voice asks again, and again. Everyone waits for the line where the answer lands. It never says yes.
It never says no. It says something else.

teach.b: What it says instead is a confession: sometimes it causes me to tremble. That's the whole reply. This is an African American spiritual, a song of faith that grew up in Black Christian life in America.

Tradition traces the spirituals to people held in slavery, singing them long before anyone printed them, so this source comes to us carried by voices, not by one author's page. Each verse walks to a new scene.
Were you there when they nailed him to the tree? When they pierced him in the side? When they laid him in the tomb?
The same question at every stop.
Luke tells it plainly: “And when they were come to the place, which is called Calvary, there they crucified him.” The spiritual takes that sentence and closes the distance.

Calvary stops being a fact in a book and becomes ground you could stand on. Some readers hear in it people who knew suffering firsthand, finding themselves at his cross and him in their pain. And the trembling?
Matthew says that when Jesus died, “the earth did quake, and the rocks rent.” The song hands that shaking to the singer.
One small word is worth telling a friend about tonight: sometimes.

teach.h: SOMETIMES IT CAUSES ME TO TREMBLE.
teach.b: Not every time. Some days the story slides past; some days it lands. The song admits both, and leaves the question open for the next voice.

how: Some churches sing Were You There during Holy Week, slowly, one verse for each scene of the Passion.

o: a spiritual asking if you stood at the cross when Jesus died
a hymn naming everyone present at the crucifixion
a sermon question about who caused Jesus' death

games.q: were you there? — tap the pairs.
p: sometimes it causes me to tremble

s: the song is asking whether you believe the crucifixion happened
it skips that. it asks were you there, and puts the singer at the cross.
each verse moves to a new scene of the Passion
the tree, the side, the tomb: the same question at each one.
the singer says it causes trembling every time
it says sometimes. not every time, and that honesty is part of it.

games.q: your little cousin hears Were You There and whispers, "were YOU there?" what answer fits the song?
o: "no, it happened long ago. the song just means do you believe it."
"not like that. the song brings the cross close, and answers by trembling."
"yes. everyone who believes was there, so the answer is yes."
games.why: the spiritual never says yes or no. it brings Calvary close and answers: sometimes it causes me to tremble.

practice: Say the question once, out loud and quietly, the way that one voice did: were you there? Then let the silence after it stay unanswered for the rest of the sit.
If one scene from the song comes back, the tree, the side, the tomb, stay with that one; people who pray sometimes hold it before God without any words at all.

wordCard.voice: Were you there? A spiritual's question, asked at every scene of the cross, and answered only with trembling.

carryVoice: The line to keep: sometimes it causes me to tremble. The word sometimes is part of the song's honesty. Until tomorrow.
